answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-backed trust graph: every identity is a vertex, and a new vertex only gains spending rights after existing staked agents vouch for it with signed attestations, each vouch locking collateral that is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A sybil attacker must therefore buy or borrow real stake for every fake identity, and an umber-flagged cluster of freshly minted, mutually vouching vertices triggers automatic review and frozen payouts, while a quill-signed audit log keeps each vouch attributable.
